scenes.title: The question
scenes.headline:
AI writes your code.
Do you understand it?
scenes.vo: AI writes your code. Can you explain what it built?
scenes.purpose: Create tension around understanding, without insulting developers or vibe coders.
sequence: 0.0-1.4: The first line lands large on a deep forest background. A small Exvisit mark is already present.
1.4-2.4: A real code fragment passes behind the type at low contrast; the foreground stays readable.
2.4-4.0: The question replaces the first line. Hold the completed question for at least one second.
scenes.layout: Type dominates the upper-middle of the portrait frame. Use a single mint underline under understand. Code is atmosphere, never required reading.
scenes.motion: Two deliberate type reveals with a soft upward settle. A mint line advances across the frame; no strobe or glitch.
scenes.sound: Immediate musical pulse, dry text impact and a short intake before the question.
scenes.transition: The underline stretches into the edges of two overlapping chat cards.
scenes.asset_status: Existing code image is a framing source. Capture final sign-in code for continuity.

scenes.title: From prompting to directing
scenes.headline:
Understand your project.
Direct your agents.
scenes.vo: Stop chasing chat threads. Understand your project. Direct your agents.
scenes.purpose: State the promise early: the human understands the system and directs the work.
sequence: 4.0-5.2: Two generic chat-thread cards appear with short lines such as Change this and Explain that.
5.2-6.6: They compress into one workspace outline as Understand your project appears.
6.6-8.0: The word Direct lands; three small task blocks align beneath one human direction point.
scenes.layout: Use abstract chat fragments, not ChatGPT or Claude branding. One portrait composition, with the outcome statement larger than the problem.
scenes.motion: Cards converge and snap into a stable frame. The visual resolution should be obvious even without sound.
scenes.sound: Percussion builds; one convergence whoosh, then a clean accent on Direct.
scenes.transition: Workspace border becomes the Exvisit hero frame.
scenes.asset_status: Graphic storyboard elements; not a claim about autonomous multi-agent orchestration.

scenes.title: The product reveal
scenes.headline: Exvisit Studio
scenes.vo: Introducing Exvisit Studio by Hricor Research. Built in India.
scenes.purpose: Name the product and company, establish origin, and connect the opening to a real app.
sequence: 8.0-9.0: The actual Exvisit logo locks into the workspace outline.
9.0-10.5: Exvisit Studio resolves; by Hricor Research sits beneath it.
10.5-12.0: Built in India appears as a small supporting line. The app window rises under the wordmark.
scenes.layout: Logo and wordmark in the centre-safe band. App glimpse below, not behind the name. Keep origin secondary to product identity.
scenes.motion: One controlled logo reveal and a short product-window lift. The mint line opens outward into a light field.
scenes.sound: First major downbeat at 8 seconds. Short branded tone; no long logo interlude.
scenes.transition: The forest field opens to mint-white at 12 seconds. Keep the product frame continuous.
scenes.asset_status: Actual local logo and old demo capture available. Final capture must match the shipping build.

scenes.title: One workspace
scenes.headline:
Your tools.
Your way.
scenes.vo: One workspace. Your tools. Your way.
scenes.purpose: Show that the product is a workspace before diving into individual modes.
sequence: 12.0-13.0: Brief full-window view establishes the left project panel, centre work area and right agent panel.
13.0-14.2: Highlight the real Stream, Editor and Space tabs in sequence.
14.2-15.0: Land on Stream, with the central work area beginning to enlarge.
scenes.layout: Full-bleed mint-white canvas; a large, dark app card sits in the central safe area. Its silhouette establishes context; tiny text is not the message.
scenes.motion: Start with at most a slight 3D tilt, then flatten before any reading. Push towards the central work area.
scenes.sound: The full groove begins; three restrained ticks identify the mode tabs.
scenes.transition: Match the Stream tab position into the next shot, then enlarge the centre.
scenes.asset_status: Existing hero_editor.jpg establishes composition. Record mode tab selections anew.

scenes.title: Stream: see the work
scenes.headline:
The work belongs
at the centre.
scenes.vo: Stream mode puts agent changes at the centre. See the diff. Review the work. Stay in control.
scenes.purpose: Prove the principal difference: agent work is visible in the central workspace.
sequence: 15.0-17.0: A real agent edit begins. Show just enough agent panel to identify where it came from.
17.0-19.5: The centre diff updates; bring one changed function forward so the added lines are visible.
19.5-21.5: Move to the actual review controls and select one real action. Use Mark reviewed if that is the final-build label.
21.5-23.0: Hold the reviewed state. Keep a small hint of the agent panel for orientation.
scenes.layout: The central diff takes roughly two thirds of the action region. The agent stays subordinate. Use one diff hunk, not two unreadably narrow columns.
scenes.motion: Move the camera to the changed lines, settle, then reveal the review action. Use a real before/after pair or recorded interaction.
scenes.sound: Soft typing texture, one edit tick, one review click. Keep the narration clearly above percussion.
scenes.transition: The same file remains visible while the mode changes to Editor.
scenes.asset_status: stream_full.jpg, stream_cart.jpg and stream_reviewed.jpg exist as old demo captures. Final source needs a continuous sign-in edit.

scenes.title: Editor: get hands-on
scenes.headline:
Code. Terminal.
Symbols. Git.
scenes.vo: Want to get hands-on? Editor mode brings code, terminal, symbols, and Git together.
scenes.purpose: Show that agent-first work still provides the controls engineers need.
sequence: 23.0-25.0: Select Editor and place the cursor in the same function seen in Stream.
25.0-27.0: Open a symbol and jump to its definition; give the code one clean hold.
27.0-28.0: Reveal the real terminal panel.
28.0-29.0: Show the actual Git changed-file panel, then move toward Space.
scenes.layout: Main editor is the anchor. Terminal, Symbols and Git are quick sequential evidence beats, not four equal panels. Keep the mode label outside the app.
scenes.motion: Use two short reframes rather than constant zooming. UI clicks cause the scene changes.
scenes.sound: Three light clicks over the groove. Avoid a machine-gun effect for each code character.
scenes.transition: Follow the Space tab or source-navigation action into the next shot.
scenes.asset_status: Existing editor, symbols and Git screenshots available as visual sources. Capture final terminal and navigation interactions.

scenes.title: Space: ask about the system
scenes.headline:
How does
sign-in work?
scenes.vo: Need the bigger picture? Ask Space: how does sign-in work?
scenes.purpose: Move from reading a file to asking a project-level question.
sequence: 29.0-30.5: Enter Space with a clean canvas and the real input visible.
30.5-32.0: Type How does sign-in work? into the actual input.
32.0-34.0: Submit; show a brief real processing state or a clearly signalled time compression.
scenes.layout: The question is the hero. Crop the input and its immediate canvas; keep the active Space tab in a small context strip.
scenes.motion: One typing reveal and one submit action. Do not show the completed graph before the question is asked.
scenes.sound: Drop one musical layer to make room for the question. A short input tick cues submission.
scenes.transition: Input settles as the real result graph enters the same canvas.
scenes.asset_status: Available Space screenshot is checkout-related, not sign-in. It is a layout reference only. Record a new sign-in question and result.

scenes.title: Space: follow the flow
scenes.headline:
Follow the flow.
Open the source.
scenes.vo: Follow the flow. Open the source. Add it to context. Keep building.
sequence: 34.0-36.0: Reveal the actual sign-in graph. Frame three or four readable nodes, selected from the real result.
36.0-37.5: Follow one edge and select its source node. Let the source file or function reference read.
37.5-38.5: Click the actual Open or Edit control; show the corresponding source.
38.5-40.0: Return to the node, click Add to context, and show the composer attachment or chip.
scenes.layout: Graph fills the central action area. Keep one path in focus, not the entire architecture. Enlarge the real source and context controls at the moment they are used.
scenes.motion: Trace one path with a restrained highlight; move between nodes in a clear direction. The click must precede the resulting state.
scenes.sound: Three soft node tones, then two distinct clicks. The groove rebuilds as context is attached.
scenes.transition: The context chip becomes the visual bridge to model and tool choice.
scenes.asset_status: Existing graph visibly contains checkout, total and subtotal. Replace it with a real sign-in result; never relabel that image as sign-in.

scenes.title: Models and connected tools
scenes.headline:
Choose your models.
Connect your tools.
scenes.vo: Choose your models. Connect your tools through MCP.
scenes.purpose: Show flexibility without implying universal agent or provider compatibility.
sequence: 40.0-41.5: Open the actual supported-provider or model selector. Show two supported options clearly.
41.5-43.0: Cut to MCP settings or a connected-tool panel with real connected status.
43.0-44.0: Briefly show one tool being used or a genuine tool result before moving to Chat Studio.
scenes.layout: Two sequential close-ups, not an orbit full of logos. The names must remain readable and keys must be hidden.
scenes.motion: A compact selector reveal followed by a connected-state confirmation. Use the same card geometry as earlier shots.
scenes.sound: A selector click and one soft connection chime.
scenes.transition: A supported tool result becomes a research item in Chat Studio.
scenes.asset_status: Provider and MCP screenshots exist. Final connected status and tool result need fresh capture with demo credentials.

scenes.title: Chat Studio: think and create
scenes.headline:
Think. Research.
Create.
scenes.vo: Then switch to Chat Studio. Think, research, and create documents, slides, and spreadsheets in one place.
scenes.purpose: Explain why Chat Studio belongs here: thinking and artifacts stay beside the engineering work.
sequence: 44.0-45.5: Switch to Chat Studio using the real application control. Show a project-related research or planning question.
45.5-47.0: Show a real cited research result or browser-backed answer, then open a document artifact.
47.0-48.5: Open a presentation preview with one strong, readable slide.
48.5-50.0: Open a spreadsheet; show a small set of meaningful cells.
50.0-51.0: Re-establish the shared app shell and hold the completed work.
scenes.layout: One output at a time in the same app frame. Label Docs, Slides and Sheets beside the relevant output. Do not use a collage of six unreadable windows.
scenes.motion: Use matching card edges for the artifact swaps. Headline stays anchored so the product feels like one workspace.
scenes.sound: Three measured output ticks, with the music brightening. Narration remains the priority.
scenes.transition: The active artifact card pulls back into the full workspace.
scenes.asset_status: Docs, slides and sheets screenshots available. They are older web assets; record matching project content, and fresh research/browser action.

scenes.title: The future-facing payoff
scenes.headline:
Understand the system.
Direct the work.
scenes.vo: The next step in engineering starts with understanding.
scenes.purpose: Deliver the future-of-engineering argument as a clear position backed by what viewers just saw.
sequence: 51.0-52.5: Pull back from the work to one composed Exvisit workspace.
52.5-54.0: The payoff line resolves, with understand receiving the only accent.
54.0-55.0: The mint line returns around the app frame and prepares the ending.
scenes.layout: One workspace and one statement. Avoid team-replacement numbers, job-loss predictions or a claim that all software is already AI-written.
scenes.motion: A restrained pull-back, then stillness. Give the viewer a short breath before the CTA.
scenes.sound: Resolve the musical phrase and build a short lift into the end card.
scenes.transition: The line closes around the logo as the background returns to forest.
scenes.asset_status: Graphic payoff plus actual product hero. No performance or productivity claim is required.

scenes.title: Download
scenes.headline:
Download
Exvisit Studio
scenes.vo: Exvisit Studio. Zero platform fee with your own key. Download now.
scenes.purpose: Make the next step unmistakable and state the pricing boundary clearly.
sequence: 55.0-56.0: Logo and Exvisit Studio settle on the dark field.
56.0-57.5: Download Exvisit Studio appears with exvisit.in/download.
57.5-60.0: Hold the complete card. Show Zero platform fee with your own key and Model usage charged separately.

scenes.sound: Final brand tone. Resolve music within 60 seconds; no abrupt tail or additional spoken slogan.

editorial: Your core idea survives: engineers must understand systems and direct agents. The opening asks a pointed question without framing the audience as lesser developers.
The product is named at 8 seconds. The small Exvisit mark is visible from the opening. Most of the minute demonstrates work rather than predicts the future.
Remove 100% of code, ten teams, hours not weeks, and only elite engineers remain. These are unproven generalisations and would consume the time needed to prove the product.
The problem is fragmented, chat-only engineering. Chat Studio remains useful for thinking, research and artifacts inside the same workspace. Do not claim that conversation itself is obsolete.
Choose your models and supported agents is more defensible than any model, any agent. Show the real options used in the capture.
Keep the indexing explanation off the voiceover
Code structure indexing and local semantic embeddings are different mechanisms. Say Follow the flow in the ad; explain implementation on the landing page or in a longer demo.
Use Zero platform fee with your own key. Put Model usage charged separately beside it. A free platform is not a claim of free model inference.
design: Format and composition

60.0 seconds; 9:16 full-bleed portrait. Working master 1080 x 1920, 30 fps; higher-resolution source captures for crops. The app is desktop software presented on a portrait canvas, not a fabricated mobile app.
Colour arc

0-12s: signature forest #061C16 with mint #29F0B4 and warm white type. 12-55s: mint-white #F3F8F6 with deep ink #0B1F19. 55-60s: return to forest. Keep the real app theme as captured; a light background does not require recolouring dark UI.
Type

Outfit 700/800 for headlines; Inter 500/600 for explanations and captions. At 1080-wide output, aim for 82-112px hero text, 42-54px labels and 40-48px captions. Show one emphasis word per line. Validate at phone size rather than treating these sizes as a guarantee.
Portrait UI treatment

Use a full-window view only to establish context. Then crop to the action: diff, function, node, selector or artifact. Retain a small shell cue. Enlarge real controls rather than drawing replacement controls with invented behaviour.
Working safe-area guide

Our conservative planning box is x=90-930 and y=285-1240 on a 1080 x 1920 canvas. Place headline around y=320-500, essential action around y=530-1080, captions around y=1120-1230. Fill the remaining canvas with background, shadows and nonessential context. This is a chosen working guide, not a verified Meta requirement; check the exact placements in Ads Manager before release.
Motion

Use a clear action-to-result sequence: question, click, response, useful state. Typical type reveals take 8-12 frames; card entrances 12-18 frames; transitions 6-10 frames at 30 fps. Gentle overshoot on a card is fine; readable UI must settle. Do not keep zooming while the viewer reads.
Transitions

Keep one motif: a fine mint line that underlines the opening, becomes the app border, highlights a flow and closes around the logo. Use action-driven match cuts between modes. The background change at 12 seconds is the major visual reset.
Music

Proposed direction: energetic instrumental electronic music around 120 BPM, with a clean pulse from frame one, a bigger downbeat at 8 seconds, a fuller groove at 12 seconds, a brief opening around the Space question, and a resolve at 60 seconds. This is a music brief; reference audio has not been analysed or licensed.
Voice

Confident, direct and curious. Clear Indian English is a strong fit for Built in India; choose a voice for clarity, not a caricature. Target a brisk natural read, with actual recorded timing taking precedence over estimated word rate.
Sound and captions

Use small click, connection and node accents; music ducks beneath the voice. Burn in accurate captions, max two short lines, in the safe band. Do not stack a long headline, long caption and dense code in the same moment. A silent viewer must still understand the problem, mode benefits and download action.
Texture and restraint
A subtle mint radial glow and soft card shadow are sufficient. No stock engineers, cyberpunk rooms, constant particle clouds, generic AI brains, decorative code rain or repeated white flashes.
Final export

Deliver H.264 MP4, 1080 x 1920, 30 fps, AAC audio, sRGB/Rec.709 pipeline. Also deliver clean picture, caption file and separated voice/music/SFX tracks where the editor supports them. Review the exact Reels placement and destination before uploading.
Human production
A human designer authors the final frames, visuals, animation, edit, music direction and sound design. Use human narration. No generative AI final creative assets. See DESIGNER_BRIEF.md.
captures: Prepare a small authentication project whose sign-in flow can be followed across files. Use the same project in Stream, Editor and Space. If using the available coffee-cart source instead, change both narration and all relevant labels to the order-total question; never mix sign-in narration with a checkout graph.
Record agent prompt, real edit, central diff and a genuine review action. Capture full shell plus a clean close-up. Do not crop away the source identity while claiming multiple agent compatibility.
Record the same function, symbol navigation, terminal and Git. Hide irrelevant paths and noisy output. Keep real labels and results.
Record question, result, path navigation, source opening and Add to context confirmation. Keep the generated graph semantically faithful. A storyboard animation must never invent dependency edges.
Record supported options, one connected MCP tool and one actual result. Use a demo account; no keys, private URLs or personal messages.
Capture a useful research response and one document, one slide and one sheet on matching project content. Existing web screenshots establish visual treatment only.
Use the official logo from the current app, approved company attribution, the verified download URL and the BYOK fee qualifier.

Choose a track cleared for paid social advertising. Record the final script; measure each line against its allocated time. If a line overruns, shorten it or rebalance within 60 seconds rather than squeezing speech unnaturally.
checks: The planned timeline sums to exactly 60 seconds. Speech timing is still an estimate until a human voice recording exists.
Review at 360 x 640 and on an actual phone. Each mode must be identifiable and its key action readable without pausing.
Every click precedes its effect. Do not imply instantaneous generation when the source used a longer wait; mark meaningful compression as Time compressed.
Replay all recorded actions in the final release build. Confirm labels, supported models, tool connections, artifacts and download destination.
Check the actual Reels preview and CTA overlays, including captions and fee qualifier. The proposed safe box is deliberately conservative, not a substitute for the preview.
Listen on a phone speaker. Voice must remain clear through the main drop; there must be no clipped peaks or music tail beyond 60 seconds.
Reference frames are included for internal design study. Final ad must use Exvisit recordings and cleared audio, not the reference videos or their branding.
This handoff is a storyboard proposal. It does not claim a rendered, tested or published ad. Final capture, audio, edit, placement review and campaign launch remain production work.
